title: FugueSpec
description: The audio PLAN, carried in show.json's `audio` field — not the score. Rev 4 of docs/fugen/phase3-audio.md deleted the runtime `fugue.json`: M68 emits a standard MIDI file, the browser loads that file, and a person opens the same file in a DAW, so review and runtime cannot disagree. What is described here is the input to that generator: the mode, the tempo, the two authored lines, and the bar-by-bar plan of where entries and episodes fall. Mirrored in Rust by crates/spex-fugue/src/model.rs.

^_.description: JSON has no comments and this document is meant to be read by a musician. A key beginning with an underscore is prose about the key beside it, ignored by every reader.

bpm.description: Beats per minute of the canonical cut. A longer cut does NOT slow the tempo — it adds episodes and entries. The music is the same music, which is the same argument resolve.rs makes about the film.

tonic.description: A full MIDI note number, not a pitch class — D4 is 62. A pitch class would need a second octave reference from somewhere else, and somewhere else is where octave errors live.

tonicLetter.description: Which letter the tonic is called, 0 = C .. 6 = B. Optional, and only needed for a black-key tonic: E-flat major and D-sharp major are the same pitches and different keys, and a pitch class cannot say which one is meant. Absent means the flat spelling, which is unambiguous for every white-key tonic including this piece's D.

subject.description: Authored, not generated — the one musical decision the piece does not delegate to an algorithm.

countersubject.description: REQUIRED as of rev 4, and required to be invertible counterpoint at the octave: a fugue exchanges its voices, and a countersubject that only works above the subject collapses the moment the parts swap. crates/spex-fugue/src/theory.rs::invertibility_faults is the check.

plan.description: Where entries, episodes and cadences fall, in bars. The generator fills in the notes and may NOT move a section off its bar: if a section cannot be realised within the contrapuntal rules it relaxes a rule and records the relaxation. The bars belong to the film.

degree.description: Zero-based scale step within the mode. Not a pitch: the whole point of a fugue is that one shape appears at different pitches, and every operation on it — transposition, inversion, the tonal answer — is diatonic.

octave.description: Whole octaves from the tonic reference. May be negative.

rest.description: A silence. Needed because a countersubject cannot cover the subject's head — the head is precisely the part that is not the same in the answer.

targetDegree.description: Where the episode LANDS: the key of the entry that follows it. Rev 1 had no such field, so an episode could modulate anywhere or nowhere. An episode that invents new material is an interlude, and that is the single easiest way for a generated fugue to stop sounding like one.
